notes: ‘A Field Guide to Grey’ — a static, strictly monochrome editorial site cataloguing the 256-step greyscale: an interactive specimen census (ARIA listbox with arrow-key walking, CIE L*, relative luminance and WCAG chips per grey, curated field notes on canonical values), the Adams/Archer Zone System mapped from CIE L* into sRGB, a live dithering laboratory (threshold, Bayer 4×4/8×8, Floyd–Steinberg and Atkinson error diffusion over procedurally drawn subjects), a WCAG contrast bench with live preview and presets, a sourced natural-history timeline, and a generated SVG plate comparing hatching, halftone and dithering. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS in three files, no dependencies, no build step, no network requests; all imagery generated at runtime via canvas and SVG; system font stacks; day/night ‘editions’ with a G keyboard shortcut and persisted preference; reduced-motion, keyboard and landmark support throughout; works from file:// and any subpath. Limitations: display and mono type rely on system fonts, so exact faces vary by platform; non-canonical specimen names are generated from 18 curated tonal bands; zone swatches are sRGB approximations of print-relative values.
